audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text states 'Mundo has zero answer to a point-and-click stun at this stage'. That is exactly backwards: his passive is an answer to a point-and-click stun.
audit.why: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, costing him health and dropping a canister he can walk over to heal and shorten its cooldown. So an empowered Ruthless Predator — the whole reason Renekton banks 50 Fury — is the ability most likely to be wasted on the passive. The correct sequencing is to spend a cheap unempowered W to strip the passive, then commit the empowered one.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text now names Goes Where He Pleases and gives the lead-with-a-cheap-W sequence; dontsFull[1].d carries the same rule in short form.
sources: enemyKit P text and hardCC flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's headline defect on this matchup is 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' — sequencingCues is 0. Heart Zapper is the tracked cooldown on every screen and its duration is never given; Maximum Dosage is never timed either.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank — the two numbers that decide when you are allowed to commit. Infected Bonesaw at 4s explains why poking him is pointless.
audit.corrected: The 17s figure is now in dosFull[0].d, phases[3].why and phases[5].why; the flat 120s is in phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 was marked Skill in both layers while the page's own whys[2] says your E-W-Q combo beats him outright there and he has no CC or burst to punish it.
audit.why: packet.levelChart gives level 3 to Renekton, and the mirror audit's chart is 'Levels 1-5 Renekton, skill from 4-5, Mundo from 6' — which also puts level 3 on Renekton. Every other row already agrees with the mirror, so this was the single disagreement.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side and win[2] flipped to Renekton together, rating raised, and phases[2].why rewritten to say why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was listed as a generic 'Executioner's Calling early' line, and dosFull[2] was titled 'Anti-heal his regen' with a description about Heart Zapper cooldowns underneath it.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags 'resistances-invalidated': Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing health and then regenerates a percent of maximum health, so stacking armour does not change the outcome — cutting the healing does. This is the one build decision that matters in the matchup and it deserved the timing, not a footnote.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now makes Grievous Wounds the plan rather than an afterthought, and dosFull[2].d finally matches its own title.
sources: enemyKit R text and percentHealth flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged "Heart Zapper's" in wants.you[2] as a probable wrong name.
audit.why: False positive — the distance of 2 is the possessive apostrophe-s. Heart Zapper is the real W name.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Dr. Mundo must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online at 3 — your E-W-Q out-trades him outright, and he has neither CC nor burst to punish the pattern.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heart Zapper's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1 — burst him inside that gap; his regen matters now but Maximum Dosage is not up yet.

edits.before: Dominus stats turn even fights into wins before 25 minutes. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s heal scaling on missing health — Dominus buys one window, and only before he presses it.

edits.before: Eclipse is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Heart Zapper's cooldown.
edits.after: His first tank item plus regen outlasts Eclipse — burst only in the 17s Heart Zapper gap.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Percent-HP damage and R regen beat any solo commit. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 — end the game instead of duelling him.

edits.before: His sustain spike + reset. Burst when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heals off stored damage on a 17s timer. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Dr. Mundo wastes Heart Zapper — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Executioner's Calling first back — his regen refunds your whole combo.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His passive eats your first stun, so lead with a cheap W first.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Eclipse  (burst + the early bully curve), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Eclipse, then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling on your first back — his regen and Maximum Dosage make Grievous Wounds the whole plan.

edits.before: E-in, empowered W-stun, Q-heal is your entire win condition — Mundo has zero answer to a point-and-click stun at this stage, take every short trade you can stack Fury for.
edits.after: E-in, empowered W-stun, Q-heal is your win condition — but Goes Where He Pleases resists the first stun and drops a canister, so lead with a cheap W and save the empowered one.

edits.before: Harass you to below 60% HP with Q cleavers so your E-W all-in heals for less and stalls out
edits.after: Open with a Blunt Force Trauma auto-reset — the wind-up is your cue to leave, not the cast

notes: The most important correction here is that spikes[0] told the reader Mundo has no answer to a point-and-click stun. Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect outright, which means a 50-Fury Ruthless Predator — the ability the whole page is built around — is the one most likely to be thrown away. The page now says to strip the passive with a cheap W first. Packet defect 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' (sequencingCues 0) is addressed with real numbers: Heart Zapper 17s at rank 1, Maximum Dosage a flat 120s at all ranks. Only one chart row disagreed with the mirror (level 3) and it is flipped in both layers together. Note that packet.levelChart gives level 6 to Skill while the mirror gives it to Dr. Mundo; I followed the mirror so the two pages agree, since the mirror explicitly rewrote that row's reasoning around Maximum Dosage.
